messages.content: I need the lodging math tightened up before we pick hotels. The flights are $936, and we decided to share one checked bag, so use $1,076 for airfare. Can you price every Savannah-and-Tybee combination with taxes and fees, then tell me which two properties to choose?

Yes. I’ll include the $318 compact car from Saturday morning through Tuesday afternoon and keep the full transportation-and-lodging ceiling at $3,800. I also still have $45 for the arrival rideshare and $90 for fuel or incidental parking. That leaves $2,271 available for all five hotel nights. Do you have exact tax rates from the listings, or should I calculate a 13% to 15% range?
Use the range first. Savannah is either $238 a night with breakfast in the historic district or $204 about a mile south. The southern place says $35 parking, but we won’t have the car until Saturday.

For Thursday and Friday nights, the historic-district hotel is $476 before tax, or $537.88 to $547.40 at 13% to 15%. The southern hotel is $408 before tax, or $461.04 to $469.20. Its parking charge should be $0 because you will not collect the car until after the two-night stay, but I’ll verify that Saturday pickup does not trigger a hotel parking fee.
Tybee is $286 beachfront plus a $32 nightly resort fee, $244 for the inn two blocks off the beach, or $219 for an apartment with a $145 cleaning fee. All are three nights.

The beachfront hotel is $858 in room charges plus $96 in resort fees, for $954 before tax. If the full amount is taxed, its total is $1,078.02 to $1,097.10. The inn is $732 before tax, or $827.16 to $841.80. The apartment is $657 plus the $145 cleaning fee, or $802 before tax; if both components are taxed, it is $906.26 to $922.30.
Show me all six combinations against the cap. I don’t want a total that quietly leaves out the rental car or those smaller transportation amounts.

Using airfare $1,076, rental car $318, arrival rideshare $45, and fuel or incidental parking $90, the non-hotel subtotal is $1,529. The six complete projected totals are: historic plus beachfront, $3,144.90 to $3,173.50; historic plus inn, $2,894.04 to $2,918.20; historic plus apartment, $2,973.14 to $2,998.70; southern plus beachfront, $3,068.06 to $3,095.30; southern plus inn, $2,817.20 to $2,840.00; and southern plus apartment, $2,896.30 to $2,920.50. Every pairing remains below $3,800.
That’s more room than I expected. Before you recommend the cheapest pair, account for breakfast and the Saturday transition. We may be out of the Savannah room before we can actually get the car.

The downtown rental counter opens at 9:00 a.m. Saturday and the quoted rate permits pickup from 9:00 to 10:00. Both Savannah hotels have 11:00 a.m. checkout, so you can collect the car before checkout if one of you stays with the bags. Both properties also confirm complimentary luggage storage for registered guests on checkout day. You could check out around 9:15, leave both bags with the desk, pick up the car together, and return to load it.
Does that create parking at either hotel when we come back for the luggage?

The historic-district hotel allows a short loading stop at its entrance without using valet parking. The southern hotel allows up to 20 minutes in its loading area after checkout, also without the $35 overnight parking charge. Neither should add a parking fee for retrieving stored bags, provided the car is not left in the guest lot.
Good. Now compare the cancellation terms. The apartment’s four-night penalty sounds disproportionate for a three-night stay.

It is. The apartment allows free cancellation only through 11:59 p.m. on October 5. After that, the penalty is four nights at the nightly rate, or $876, even though this reservation would be for three nights; the cleaning fee is refunded if the stay never begins. The beachfront hotel is refundable through 6:00 p.m. on October 11, then charges one night plus the resort fee and applicable tax. The Tybee inn is refundable through 4:00 p.m. on October 16, then charges the full three-night stay.
And the two Savannah places?

The historic-district hotel can be canceled without charge through 6:00 p.m. on October 15. After that it charges one night plus tax. The southern hotel’s deadline is 3:00 p.m. on October 14, followed by a two-night room-and-tax penalty. The historic hotel gives you one additional day and a substantially smaller late-cancellation exposure.
So the southern hotel saves around $77, but it has no breakfast and worse cancellation. Is that the right comparison?

Correct. At the high end of the tax range, it saves $78.20 over two nights. The historic hotel includes breakfast for two on both mornings, has the more useful cancellation deadline, and places you in the historic district before you have a car. Unless breakfast would be worth very little to you, the savings from moving south are modest.
For Tybee, is there any financial reason to take the apartment over the inn?

No. The apartment is projected to cost about $79 to $95 more than the inn after its cleaning fee, and its cancellation exposure starts much earlier. Its practical advantage is apartment space and a kitchen, not price. The inn is also roughly $251 to $255 below the beachfront hotel while being two blocks from the beach and avoiding a resort fee.
What are the actual totals if we choose the historic hotel and the inn? Give me a conservative number and what remains for price movement.

Using 15% as the conservative tax assumption, the historic hotel is $547.40 and the Tybee inn is $841.80, so lodging is $1,389.20. Adding airfare $1,076, rental $318, rideshare $45, and fuel or incidental parking $90 produces a complete projected total of $2,918.20. That leaves $881.80 below the $3,800 ceiling.
One correction: I found the checkout screens. Savannah tax is 14%, and the inn total already shown is $829.56, including tax. Can you replace the range with the real total?

At 14%, the historic hotel is $476 plus $66.64 tax, totaling $542.64. With the inn’s displayed total of $829.56, lodging is $1,372.20. The complete trip projection becomes $2,901.20: airfare $1,076, Savannah hotel $542.64, Tybee inn $829.56, rental car $318, arrival rideshare $45, and fuel or incidental parking $90. The remaining cushion is $898.80.
Choose those two, then. Summarize the dates, luggage plan, pickup timing, and cancellation deadlines so I can book from the right screens. Don’t treat anything as booked yet.

Select the historic-district hotel for Thursday, October 17 through Saturday, October 19, at $542.64 including 14% tax, and the Tybee inn for Saturday, October 19 through Tuesday, October 22, at the displayed $829.56 total. On Saturday, check out around 9:15 a.m. and leave the bags with the hotel, collect the compact car from the downtown counter during the 9:00-10:00 a.m. pickup window, then use the hotel’s loading area to retrieve the luggage without a parking charge. The Savannah hotel is refundable through 6:00 p.m. October 15; the Tybee inn is refundable through 4:00 p.m. October 16. The projected transportation-and-lodging total is $2,901.20, leaving $898.80 under the $3,800 cap. These are the selected booking screens only; flights, hotels, and car remain unbooked.
